title: Waiting for the 'Perfect Time' to Invest Costs $163K
hook: You got a bonus and swore you'd invest it 'when things calmed down' — that instinct has been studied, named, and it has a six-figure price tag.
angle: 60% of investors hold cash waiting for the 'right moment' to invest. Behavioral economists call it cash drag. The average delay is 14 months. On $50K that's $4,100 in missed growth — and over a 30-year career, five of those delays compound into $163,000 gone. Vanguard's own research shows lump-sum investing beats 'wait for a dip' 68% of the time.
audience: Savers and earners who have money sitting in a checking account they keep meaning to invest 'soon'
key_numbers: 60% of investors hold cash waiting for the right time
68% of the time lump-sum beats waiting for a dip
$163,000 lost over a 30-year career from repeated delays
